# 7-day sample menu: stages 1 and 2

--8<-- "includes/starting-points.md"

At stages 1 and 2 the kidneys still filter well, so there is no potassium or phosphorus limit unless your blood tests run high. The goals are the ones that slow kidney disease: sodium under 2,000 mg, protein that is enough but not too much (56–70 g for a 70 kg adult, and never more than 1.3 g per kg), and a plant-forward pattern with vegetables, fruit, whole grains, beans and nuts. This week has fish, poultry or lean beef at one meal on most days, one meat-free day, at least 14 g of fiber per 1,000 kcal and about 55 g of carbohydrate at each main meal. Potassium and phosphorus are shown for information.

## The numbers this menu is built to

Built for a reference adult: 70 kg, 170 cm, type 1 diabetes, using the app's starting targets for **G1** (see [Eating well](../index.md#your-numbers)). Every day below was checked against these numbers by `scripts/build_handbook.py`.

| Per day | Built to |
|---|---|
| Protein | 56–70 g (0.8–1.0 g/kg) |
| Sodium | at most 2,000 mg |
| Potassium | no limit (shown for information) |
| Phosphorus | no limit (shown for information) |
| Energy from food | 1,750–2,450 kcal |
| Carbohydrate | about 55 g at each main meal (every meal 50–60 g); snacks 10–30 g |
| Fiber | at least 14 g per 1,000 kcal |

Also: no foods with phosphate additives.

## Swaps that keep the numbers

- **Beans and lentils** swap ½ cup for ½ cup: each has about 20 g carbohydrate and 7–9 g protein.
- **Whole grains** swap at the same carbohydrate: ¾ cup brown rice (39 g), 1 cup whole-wheat pasta (35 g), 1 cup quinoa (39 g), 1 cup oatmeal (28 g).
- **Fish or chicken for beans:** 2 oz of cooked chicken has about 18 g protein and no carbohydrate, so add a starch to keep the meal's carbohydrate steady, and keep the day under 70 g of protein.
- **Nuts:** almonds and walnuts swap ounce for ounce. Choose unsalted.

## Make it yours

- **Scale for your weight.** Protein here is 0.8–1.0 g per kg for 70 kg: 48–60 g a day at 60 kg and 64–80 g at 80 kg. Keep it under 1.3 g per kg. Ask your dietitian which weight to use.
- **If a blood test shows high potassium or phosphate,** your team may ask you to limit them; the [stage 3 menu](g3.md) shows how a limited week looks.
- **Carbohydrate stays steady:** about the same amount at each main meal every day, so a fixed insulin plan or a carbohydrate ratio works the same way from day to day. Your own amount per meal comes from your diabetes team; keep it consistent and count what you actually eat ([Carb counting](../carb-counting.md)).
- **Lows come first.** Treat a low straight away with glucose tablets or another fast 15 g ([Treating a low](../../t1d/treating-a-low.md)), even if it adds potassium or fluid. Rescue foods are on top of these menus and are never "against the rules".
- **Hungry, or losing weight without trying?** Add calories with olive oil, unsalted butter or more measured starch covered by your usual insulin plan, not with more meat, and tell your dietitian ([Eating enough](../eating-enough.md)).
- **Season without salt:** herbs, spices, garlic and onion powder, lemon and vinegar. Do not use salt substitutes: they contain potassium chloride ([Sodium](../sodium.md)).
- **Log it in the app:** every food here is in the app's food list under the same name. Saved meals and "copy day" let you reuse a menu day ([Planning and menus](../../app/planning-and-menus.md)).

## Sources

- [USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy)][FDC]: every nutrient value, through the app's food list.
- [KDOQI 2020 nutrition guideline][Q20]: energy 25–35 kcal/kg (statement 3.1.1) and protein (statements 3.0.1–3.0.4).
- [KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline][K24]: sodium under 2 g a day (Rec 3.3.2.1); protein 0.8 g/kg and avoid more than 1.3 g/kg (PP 3.3.1.1); limit potassium only when it runs high (PP 3.11.5.2).
- [KDIGO 2022 diabetes in CKD guideline][K22]: a diet high in vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fiber and legumes (practice point 3.1.1).
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 11][A26-11]: protein 0.8 g/kg with diabetes and CKD before dialysis, 1.0–1.2 g/kg on dialysis (Rec 11.3).
- [ADA Standards of Care 2026, section 5][A26-5]: at least 14 g fiber per 1,000 kcal (Rec 5.24) and consistent carbohydrate on fixed insulin plans (Rec 5.28).
- [NKF: carbohydrate counting with CKD][DG7]: 15 g is one carbohydrate choice; 3–6 choices per meal, set by your dietitian.
